derived.method: (31,639,412 Class A beneficially owned + 9,444,375 Class B) / (3,729,400,000 Class A + 9,444,375 Class B outstanding at the April 8, 2025 record date) = 1.10%. Computed, not stated in the filing. Caveats: his holdings are as of February 28, 2025 while the share counts are as of April 8, 2025; his Class A figure includes 6,726,161 shares under options exercisable within 60 days and 392,106 shares under stock units vesting within 60 days, which are not in the outstanding count; and it includes shares owned by his spouse, a family charitable foundation and family trusts. Cross-check: proxy footnote 8 says that if he converted his Class B into Class A 'he would beneficially own approximately 1% of the Class A common stock.'

structure.note: Two voting classes. Holders of Class A common stock have 66 2/3% of the voting power and holders of Class B common stock have 33 1/3%, which is generally non-dilutable. Each Class B share has 15 votes; at the April 8, 2025 record date each Class A share had 0.07597 votes. Brian L. Roberts beneficially owns all 9,444,375 Class B shares through a limited liability company of which he is the managing member, giving him 33 1/3% of the combined vote. That is below 50%, so the company is not majority-controlled on these figures. Class B is convertible share for share into Class A.

notes: Fiscal year ended December 31, 2024 (matches data.js fy 'Dec 2024'). Ownership is from the 2025 proxy (filed April 25, 2025). ROBERTS: the proxy gives his Class A stake only as '*' (less than 1% of Class A), his Class B as 100% of the class, and 33 1/3% of combined voting power, so pctVoting is 33.33 and the all-shares figure is the documented derived 1.10% (see derived.method). His 31,639,412 Class A shares include 286,044 owned by his spouse, 1,032,645 owned by a family charitable foundation of which his spouse is a trustee, and 16,767,579 owned by certain family trusts. Relation is 'ceo' (data.js role 'Chair and CEO'); the filings read here do not describe him as a founder. HOLDERS: the Vanguard and BlackRock percentages are of Class A common stock, not of all shares; Class B is 9,444,375 shares against 3,729,400,000 Class A at the record date, so the difference is small, but the figures are not recomputed. Both rest on Schedule 13G/A filings reporting holdings as of December 31, 2023, so they are stale. BUYBACKS: the cash-flow line ($9,103m) includes repurchases under employee plans and excise tax; the 10-K says Comcast repurchased 212 million Class A shares for $8.6 billion under its authorization in 2024. STOCK COMP: the cash-flow add-back is $1,288m; Note 12 reports share-based compensation expense of $1,069m. The cash-flow figure is used for consistency with the other records; the note does not reconcile the two.
